thread:
maya: seeing a surge of 502/503s hitting model-store in us-west-2 around 02:10 UTC. a bunch of nodes in the gpu pool started failing healthchecks.
jon: same here, dashboards show NAT Gateway 5xx spike and high active connections on the nodes.
maya: suspect ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT. if model workers open lots of short-lived outbound connections (S3/ECR), nat can run out.
liam: can you paste the CloudWatch graph? also are we doing parallel model pulls from each node during the rollout?
maya: attaching small snippet from CloudWatch (summarized): NAT ActiveConnections spiked ~15k -> plateaued; NatErrors (PortExhaustion) alarms fired.
anya: from VPC flow logs I can see a flood of SYNs to S3 endpoints and ECR in the same time window. lots of client-side retries too.
jon: ran "ss -s" on a couple of affected nodes, shows tons of TIME-WAIT and high ephemeral port usage. ephemeral range is default 32768-60999.
maya: here's the output I grabbed:
```
$ ss -tan | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l
12890
$ sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 32768	60999
```
liam: ok that explains it. each node can only open ~28k concurrent ephemeral sockets then hit reuse/TIME_WAIT. with aggressive parallel downloads during rollout we ACEed the nat.
anya: AWS NAT Gateway is per-AZ and scales but you still hit port exhaustion because SNAT ports are shared per NAT gw public IP. We have 2 nat-gw in az-1, one in az-2. most traffic was originating from az-1.
maya: root cause summary: rollout triggered concurrent model pulls from many pods across nodes in same AZ, causing many short-lived outbound connections -> ephemeral port depletion on the NAT -> egress failures -> healthcheck flapping.
jon: immediate mitigation applied: throttled rollout concurrency, paused the rollout, scaled NAT by adding an extra NAT Gateway in az-1 and added an EIP, and pushed a quick config to prefer multi-AZ pod spreading.
sre-bot: incident: nat-ephemeral-port-exhaustion_us-west-2 created by maya at 02:22 UTC. runbook: reduce parallelism, add nat gateways, use VPC endpoints for S3/ECR, widen local port range, or move heavy egress to dedicated instances.
liam: medium-term fixes we discussed:
- add S3 and ECR VPC endpoints to cut egress to the internet
- switch large model pulls to use a shared sidecar that multiplexes downloads (reduce connection count)
- increase ip_local_port_range to 15000-65535 on worker AMI, plus tune tcp_tw_reuse/tcp_tw_recycle (careful with recycling)
- introduce per-node egress ENIs (NAT per ENI pattern) or use NAT instances to control SNAT ports
- ensure rollout controller does pod-spread across AZs and rate-limits concurrent start for model-heavy pods
anya: also recommend enabling enhanced flow logs for the time window and exporting conntrack dumps from nodes to verify reuse patterns.
maya: follow-ups: liam/anya to run a small controlled repro next week to measure threshold and update runbook. jon to update the deployment strategy to 10% per minute and prefer az-distribution.
jon: noted. will push the charted concurrency limits and add automated rollback threshold if >5% egress errors in 5m.
maya: checklist done for now. will close once we have VPC endpoints + rollout config in prod and observability dashboards for ephemeral usage.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-concurrency-limits v2 -> staging at 05:10 UTC (manual gate for prod). :robot_face:
liam: thanks everyone. lesson: high parallelism + short-lived egress = NAT port risk, treat S3/ECR as internal when possible.
maya: closing thread with action items. will create a follow-up doc with measurements and exact sysctl recommendations.
